answer: Make standing perishable, renewed only by continuous fresh work. An identity's weight decays exponentially each epoch toward zero and is topped up solely by newly graded contributions, so influence is a pigment that fades unless repainted every dawn. A farm cannot mint a thousand fakes once and let them idle — dormant personas bleed to nothing within a few half-lives, and the inlet to real standing demands ongoing per-identity labor forever. Upkeep scales with headcount continuously, not as a one-time fee, so breadth becomes a permanent recurring tax rather than a sunk cost.
